title: System-Wide Roofline Profiling -a Case Study on NERSC's Perlmutter Supercomputer
problem: Individual application profiling leaves critical gaps in understanding total system utilization on large-scale HPC systems. Hardware design trends emphasizing reduced-precision operations and memory bandwidth may not align with actual scientific workload characteristics.
motivation: HPC system architects need quantitative empirical understanding of actual system-wide workload behavior to guide hardware-software co-design decisions.
method: They measured actual GPU activity across thousands of processors in NERSC's Perlmutter supercomputer while it ran real scientific workloads. They used roofline analysis—a method that identifies whether a machine is bottlenecked by computing power or memory bandwidth—to map where each workload fell. They measured both how precisely numbers were stored and how much actual computation happened per chunk of data fetched from memory, then compared these against the machine's physical limits.
key_novelty: They applied roofline analysis across an entire supercomputer's GPU population running real production workloads, rather than testing individual applications in isolation.
contributions: Empirical characterization showing FP64 dominates scientific computing at 66% of flops, with FP32 at 33% and FP16 rare
Quantitative evidence that 54% of workload is compute-bound and 46% is bandwidth-bound, showing near-equal distribution
Methodology for large-scale system-wide performance profiling leveraging hardware metrics from production systems
Empirical evidence contradicting hardware design trends that emphasize reduced-precision and prioritize compute over memory bandwidth

metrics.other: FP precision distribution (FP64: 66%, FP32: 33%, FP16: rare); arithmetic intensity: 46% bandwidth-bound, 54% compute-bound

limitations: Results are specific to Perlmutter's architecture; generalizability to other HPC systems and future architectures not discussed.
primary_theme: System-wide performance characterization via roofline analysis
